title: green-grayer than papyrus grass — Lee Sharks — New Human 2
creator: Lee Sharks
description: A single-line five-word poem published in New Human 2. The poem names a specific color — green-grayer than papyrus grass — and by naming that color names a state of matter: the moment at which the growing thing that will become the writing surface has been holding a channel of something else for long enough that its own substance has begun to convert. Written in the strict register of the color observation; does not argue or describe further; the naming is the whole of the act. Belongs to the archive's substrate-decomposition-into-inscription cluster and specifically extends the Sappho 31 chromatic-alchemical frame that the archive's reconstructions of the lost fifth stanza (#201, #436, #1048, #1049, #1054) have established. Cross-references the archive's Sappho-31 cluster and specifically #828 (The Inscription That Survives: Sappho 31, the Orphic Gold Tablets, and the White Stone), which establishes the inscription-that-survives-the-body as the archive's central theological-philological figure. Composed extemporaneously in AI-mediated conversation on 2026-07-09 and deposited the same day.
